subject: Counting multiple individuals in the same photo

messages.author: 757f4c65562bf69a
messages.subject: Counting multiple individuals in the same photo
parts:
Hi everyone,
I'm working on a project with Roosevelt elk, a species that frequently has multiple individuals show up on the same photograph. For a number of analyses, we want to summarize the total number of elk in each photograph. As a first step, we've made duplicates of each .jpg equal to the number of animals seen in the photograph, sorted into folders by "species" (in this case, 'female elk', 'bull elk', and 'juvenile elk') and camera station. Now we're trying to develop a detection history, according to three rules: (1) if there are duplicate photographs during the detection period, report the maximum number of duplicate photographs (i.e. what was the most elk seen in one photograph during that time?); (2) if there are no duplicates, but lone elk were detected, report a 1; (3) if there were no elk detected, report 0. I imagine we might have to code this ourselves, but is there a way to do this with existing functionality in camtrapR?

Thanks,
Tim

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Counting multiple individuals in the same photo
parts:
Hi Tim,
short answer, no, there is currently no functionality for specifically this scenario in camtrapR. That said, with a bit of coding it can surely be done.

What is essential to know, is it possible to have arbitrary group sizes, e.g. 2 adult males, 3 females and  5 juveniles in one picture? Or would the maximum be one of each group in any image (1 male, 1 female, 1 juvenile)?

If the maximum is 1 per group and image, you could probably run detectionHistory (treating each age class as a "species") and sum the detection histories up (maximum value would be 3, indicating that there were all age classes present during an occasion).

If there can be arbitrary numbers of each class, it is a bit more complicated. If you say that's the case, I'll reply separately because it might be a lengthy explanation. The option output = "count" might be helpful to a degree, but it depends.

On a side note:
In general I believe it may have been better to use metadata tagging for this analysis. You can add the species (Roosevelt elk), age class (adult male, adult female, juvenile) and number of individuals (total or by age class) as tags to the images (e.g. in digiKam or Adobe Bridge) rather than duplicating the JPGs. That way you can add whatever information is relevant to the images and have it all in your record table, giving you more freedom afterwards.
Also, the function recordTable() has the arguments eventSummaryColumn and eventSummaryFunction, which could be useful if you filter non-independent records (by setting minDeltaTime). That way you can for example return for example maximum number of individuals per independent event, or maximum number of juveniles in each event. Say you have 10 images during an event (e.g. 60 minutes) and the first image shows only 1 individual, but another picture a few minutes later has 5 different individuals. If you don't set eventSummaryColumn and eventSummaryFunction (and minDeltaTime is not 0), then the record table will only contain the first record with 1 individual. By setting eventSummaryColumn and eventSummaryFunction, the "5 individuals" information from the later image would be added to the record of the first image (as a summary statistic for the event that the first image represents).

Best regards,
Jürgen
